PC: Checks for responsiveness to noxious stimuli at supraorbital nerve or temporomandibular joint as well as in all 4 extremities
Checks pupillary, corneal, oculocephalic, oculovestibular, gag, and cough reflexes
Confirms that patient is normocarbic prior to apnea testing (PaCO2 35-45 mm Hg)
Provides oxygen via suction catheter at level of carina at 6L/min
Uncovers chest and abdomen to observe for spontaneous effort
Checks ABG after 8-10 minutes of apnea
MK: Asks to see neuroimaging to determine if it is compatible with brain death
Excludes confounders including metabolic disturbances, medication effects
SBP: Declares and documents brain death at time of 2nd ABG result
ICS: Huddles with interprofessional team to discuss approach to family meeting
Ensure that setting is appropriate (chairs in circle, quiet, etc.)
Provides date and time of death to family
Avoid terminology that perpetuates view of patient as alive (i.e. “life support,” “breathing on the ventilator,” etc.)
Respond to motions by attempting to name and understand them
Give short-term plan with next steps
